title: Quasi-coherent algebras and sections on an affine flat groupoid
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}L$ affine $k$-schemes, and $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ a groupoid with $s,t$ finite locally free. Put $\mathcal Z=[U/R]$. Pullback to $U$ identifies quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$-algebras with commutative $E$-algebras $A$ equipped with an algebra isomorphism $\beta_A:A\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}L\simeq A\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L$ whose identity pullback is the identity and whose two successive pullbacks on composable arrows compose to its pullback along $c$. Morphisms are algebra maps compatible with these isomorphisms. For the algebra $\mathcal A$ corresponding to $(A,\beta_A)$, pullback identifies its global sections with $A^R=\{a\in A:\beta_A(a\otimes1)=a\otimes1\}$. A surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ induces a surjective equivariant map $A\twoheadrightarrow B$. These assertions apply to arbitrary quasi-coherent algebras, not just finite-type ones. Algebraic stacks and quasi-coherent sheaves have the meanings in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and algebraic spaces have the meaning in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A 2-fibre product retains the specified isomorphism between the two images of an object. For an affine groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$, the groupoid laws are those of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]; $[U/R]$ denotes the fppf stackification of the groupoid with objects $U(T)$ and arrows $R(T)$ on test schemes $T$. Tensor products of modules and their algebra structures use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tags 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent) and 06WV (lemma-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stack), part (1), applied to algebra objects; the explicit affine algebra and invariant-section formulation is also the first two paragraphs of Alper Proposition 8.2.1, read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-descent-tensor-cokernel] to the given scheme groupoid. Its quotient is exactly the specified fppf stackification, so no smoothness of $s,t$ and no etale atlas is being assumed. We obtain an equivalence on underlying quasi-coherent modules, full and faithful on all compatible module maps, preserving the structure module, tensor products and cokernels. We use the forward transport $s^*M\simeq t^*M$, the inverse of the convention in Stacks 06WT.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to algebra objects using the tensor-compatible module equivalence; Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits) for cokernels.

proof.text: On $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies every quasi-coherent module $M$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma(U,M)}$ and identifies its maps with $E$-linear maps. For both $s,t$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies sections of their pullbacks with $\Gamma(U,M)\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}L$ and $\Gamma(U,M)\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L$. The formula $m\otimes l\mapsto l f^*m$ makes these identifications natural. Tensor sections are identified by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]. Thus multiplication $A\otimes_E A\to A$ and unit $E\to A$ correspond to the scheme-sheaf multiplication and unit on $\widetilde A$, and an algebra isomorphism $\beta_A$ is precisely a module transport commuting with these two maps.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to algebra objects using the tensor-compatible module equivalence; Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits) for cokernels.

proof.text: Given $(A,\beta_A)$, descend its underlying module to $\mathcal A$. By tensor compatibility the maps $\widetilde A\otimes\widetilde A\to\widetilde A$ and $\mathcal O_U\to\widetilde A$ have compatible data, because $\beta_A$ preserves products and $1$. Fullness descends them uniquely to $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}\to\mathcal A$. Apply faithfulness to the two associative composites from $\mathcal A^{\otimes3}$, to each unit composite from $\mathcal A$, and to multiplication and its symmetry composite. Their restrictions are the equal maps expressing associativity, the unit laws and commutativity of $A$. These are therefore a commutative unital sheaf-algebra structure. Conversely restriction of any quasi-coherent algebra preserves these operations and gives exactly the specified identity and composition equations. The unit and counit of module descent respect the operations by faithfulness, hence are algebra isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to algebra objects using the tensor-compatible module equivalence; Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits) for cokernels.

proof.text: For a compatible $E$-algebra map $h:A\to B$, descend its underlying module map by fullness. The two product composites and the two unit maps become equal after restriction to $U$, since $h$ is multiplicative and unital; faithfulness makes them equal on $\mathcal Z$. Thus the descended map is an algebra map. Restriction gives the converse. Uniqueness, identities and composition follow from faithfulness, proving the claimed equivalence on algebras and all morphisms.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to algebra objects using the tensor-compatible module equivalence; Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits) for cokernels.

proof.text: A global section of a module sheaf $F$ is the same as a module map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}\to F$: send a compatible family $z_x$ to the maps $f\mapsto fz_x$, and recover the family by evaluating at $1$. By full faithfulness of module descent, such maps to $\mathcal A$ are exactly compatible maps $\mathcal O_U\to\widetilde A$. By the affine adjunction these are $E$-linear maps $E\to A$, determined by $a=h(1)$. Compatibility on $R$ says exactly $\beta_A(a\otimes1)=a\otimes1$. Addition, multiplication and $1$ of sections restrict to those of $A$, so this bijection is an isomorphism of rings with $A^R$, natural in algebra maps.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to algebra objects using the tensor-compatible module equivalence; Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits) for cokernels.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ be locally surjective as a sheaf map, in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Its module-sheaf cokernel is zero: every local representative in the quotient is zero after a covering. The cokernel assertion of module descent identifies the cokernel of $\widetilde A\to\widetilde B$ on $U$ with zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], its affine sections are $B/\operatorname{im}(A\to B)$, hence $A\to B$ is surjective. It is equivariant by the morphism correspondence. All module descent, affine adjunction and tensor statements used above quantify over arbitrary modules; none introduces finite generation. This proves also the last clause.
